sourceChecks: creation-psychology: explicit demand that competing malicious motives be ruled out or shown less probable is not accompanied by comparable screening of loving motives; the source-specific unequal standard is already described in the critique.

mixed-world-counterexample: after the request for a corresponding positive mirror, the reply returns to a worst mixed-world example, leaving the narrower comparison unanswered; the critique already records this diversion.

definitionChecks.label: Special pleading
definitionChecks.definition: Applying an exception or different standard to one side of the argument without giving a principled reason for the difference.
definitionChecks.decision: Accepted for the bounded initial unequal creation-motive demand, not for every conditional asymmetry claim or probability question.

definitionChecks.label: Red herring
definitionChecks.definition: Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.
definitionChecks.decision: Accepted only for the post-clarification mixed-world reply; the earlier counterexample remains a relevant response, not a retrospective diversion.

rejectionReview: Read all eighty decisions and both complete primary candidate tables. Openly declared conceptions, conditional claims, admitted uncertainty, explicit reframing and acknowledged contrary evidence were not converted into circularity, equivocation, ignorance or bias merely because further support is needed. No distinct cognitive-bias mechanism passed the exact local definitions.
